results.body:
Law Society of Alberta trust report

Law firms registered with the Law Society of Alberta that operate trust accounts are required to file a Trust Safety Accounting Upload as part of their annual reporting to the Law Society of Alberta. Annual reporting for each year is due by March 31st of the following year. As an approved vendor of the Law Society of Alberta, Clio makes it easy to fulfill the accounting and reporting requirements set forth by the Law Society of Alberta. Compliance remains a shared responsibility between Clio and your law firm, so refer to the Law Society Annual Reporting web page for additional details about annual reporting.

Enable Law Society of Alberta reports

All law firms where the Clio account’s mailing address is in Canada should automatically have Law Society of Alberta reports enabled. Find your firm's mailing address in Settings > Account and Payment Info. If you operate in Alberta, but your account’s mailing address is not in Canada, the account’s Primary subscriber or an Administrator can contact Clio customer support to request for these reports to be enabled. Once enabled, the following information fields that were previously optional will now be required.

Institution

When creating a trust account in Clio Manage, enter the name of the institution (bank) where the actual funds are held. You can enter any institution name, but the Law Society of Alberta expects one of the following institutions:

▪️ Alberta Credit Union ▪️ ATB Financial ▪️ Bank of Nova Scotia ▪️ BMO ▪️ CIBC ▪️ Canadian Western Bank ▪️ Central 1 Credit Union ▪️ CIBC ▪️ Citibank ▪️ Fargo ▪️ Desjerdins Caisses ▪️ Calgary Financial ▪️ HSBC ▪️ ING Direct ▪️ Lakehead ▪️ Laurentian ▪️ Manulife ▪️ National Bank of Canada ▪️ President's Choice ▪️ RBC ▪️ Servus Credit Union ▪️ TD Canada Trust ▪️ Credit Union (other) ▪️ Other

Payment method

When disbursing trust funds, enter the payment method. The Law Society of Alberta expects one of the following payment methods:

▪️ Service Fee ▪️ Bank Draft ▪️ Cash ▪️ Cheque ▪️ Credit card ▪️ Debit card ▪️ Direct Deposit ▪️ Direct Withdrawal ▪️ Wire Transfer ▪️ Email Transfer ▪️ Transfer to General ▪️ Money Order ▪️ Other

Type

When depositing trust funds, enter the payment type. The Law Society of Alberta expects one of the following types:

▪️ Service Fee ▪️ Bank Draft ▪️ Cash ▪️ Cheque ▪️ Credit card ▪️ Debit card ▪️ Direct Deposit ▪️Direct Withdrawal ▪️ Wire Transfer ▪️ Email Transfer ▪️ Transfer to General ▪️ Money Order ▪️ Other

Practice area

When creating a new matter, select the practice area in the Matter details section. The Law Society of Alberta expects one of the following practice areas:

▪️ Aboriginal ▪️ Administrative/Boards/Tribunals ▪️ Arbitration ▪️ Bankruptcy/Insolvency/Receivership ▪️ Civil Litigation ▪️ Commercial ▪️ Corporate ▪️ Criminal ▪️ Employment/Labour ▪️ Entertainment ▪️ Environmental ▪️ Estate Planning and Administration ▪️ Immigration ▪️ Intellectual Property  ▪️ International ▪️ Matrimonial/Family ▪️ Mediation ▪️ Mortgage ▪️ Personal Injury ▪️ Real Estate/Conveyancing ▪️ Tax ▪️ Other

Note: If your default list for Practice area does not include a list item that you need to use, add or edit practice areas via your Settings > Firm Preferences.

Tip: If you’ve recently enabled the Law Society of Alberta reports and want to know which of your matters do not have practice areas assigned, go to Matters and sort the table by Practice area. Matters without a practice area will show up at the top of the table. You can edit each matter until all matters have practice areas assigned.

Responsible attorney

When creating a new matter, select the responsible attorney from the list of practicing attorneys at your firm. To appear in the list of attorneys to select from, an attorney must be a Clio user on your firm’s account.

Note: Make sure that each attorney that operates a trust fund has their Law Society of Alberta Member ID entered in the Lawyer registered number field in their profile (Settings > Profile). When Law Society of Alberta reporting has been enabled, this field will be available in the profiles of all users who have their Subscriber Type field set as Attorney.

Tip: If you’ve recently enabled the Law Society of Alberta reports and want to know which of your matters do not have a responsible attorney, go to Matters and sort the table by Responsible attorney. Matters without a responsible attorney will show up at the top of the table. You can edit each matter until all matters have a responsible attorney.

To minimize the risk of reporting issues, make sure to consistently fill required fields with information expected by the Law Society of Alberta.

 

Disable Law Society of Alberta reports

The Primary subscriber or an Administrator on the Clio Manage account can disable these reports.

  1. Go to Settings > Firm Preferences.
  2. Select the Compliance subtab.
  3. Uncheck LSA report is enabled.

 

Generate a Law Society of Alberta report

  1. In Clio Manage, go to Reports > Reports.
  2. Select the report category Compliance.
  3. Click LSA reports.
  4. Select the relevant calendar year, then click Generate report. Four links will be generated. Click on each link to download the following CSV files:
    • AL: This file summarizes the Accounts Receivables balances (by matter) as of December 31st. The file includes unpaid time, unpaid expenses, and taxes on a per-matter basis for the selected report year. A client will appear in this report if they have transactions in their trust account and at least one unpaid bill.
    • TT: This file summarizes all trust account transactions for the specified report year. This includes receipts/deposits, withdrawals, and matter-to-matter transfers.
    • BAR: This file summarizes the Billing Journal (by matter) for the reporting period. It includes all bill payments, credit notes, and outstanding amounts for the selected report year.
    • TL: This section includes the opening trust balance for each matter for the selected report year.

Review each downloaded CSV file for any missing information, typos, or non-standard entries in the fields required by the Law Society of Alberta. To prevent mismatched information between data in Clio Manage and CSV files submitted to the Law Society of Alberta, update any problematic information in Clio Manage, then regenerate the Law Society of Alberta report. If you make any edits to your CSV files, make sure to save your changes and ensure that the file format is saved as a CSV file before submitting these files to the Law Society of Alberta.

Note: The Practice area, Payment method, and Responsible attorney fields in Clio Manage correspond to the Area of Law Description, Method of Payment, and Responsible Lawyer Name columns in the CSV files, respectively.

 

Other Law Society of Alberta best practices

Time Entries: The Law Society of Alberta recommends against using negative time entries to “add credit” to a client account. In Clio Manage, you can instead add a credit note to a user’s account.

results.name: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.title: Clio Manage Client Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Client reports provide a comprehensive overview of client balances, bank account and matter transaction history, non-billable and billable work in progress, and trust account balances. On matters with multiple clients, most reports apply to the default client only. The Matter balance summary, Trust management, Invoice payments, Client Ledger, and Trust Listing reports support multiple clients on a matter.

See below for a summary of each client report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.

Client activity report

The client activity report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of billed and unbilled time and expense activities across matters. This report does not include non-billable time. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

Activity type

This column shows whether the recorded activity is a time entry or expense entry.

Status

This column shows whether the activities are billed or unbilled. Activities are divided by billed and unbilled status, with billed activities appearing first with their subtotal, followed by unbilled activities.

User

This column lists the firm user who created the activity entry.

Activity category

This column shows the activity category recorded when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Description

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses for the listed activity.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for the matter.

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for each of a client's matters.

Billed total

This total is the summarized total cost of billed time and expense entries for all of a client's matters.

 

Client ledger report

The client ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed view of client trust and operating transactions. This report also shows payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust ledger report

The trust ledger report is designed to give firms a detailed breakdown of client and matter transactions and balances across all trust accounts. The report includes payments, refunds, transfers, and balances. You can use this report to submit to regulators. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Payer/Payee

This column shows information about the person making or receiving a payment. This information is useful when the payer or payee is not the client themselves.

Reference

This column shows data entered in the Reference field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field from when you recorded a new transaction.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Client total

This lists the total balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance for all of the client's matters. If you have transactions across multiple operating and trust accounts, you may see different balances.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Trust interest calculation report

The trust interest calculation report is designed to calculate interest earned on deposited client matter trust funds across all trust accounts. You can use this report to calculate interest for trust funds based on rate, compounding period, and date range for a specific client or matter. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the IOLTA account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists trust funds deposited into the IOLTA account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money remaining after each listed transaction.

Rate

This column lists the selected interest rate for each deposit.

Balance start date

The start date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Balance end date

The end date of the interest period as per the date range you selected to generate the report.

Days held

This column shows the total number of days of the interest period you selected to generate the report.

Interest

This column shows the amount of interest accrued based on the balance for the selected period.

A summary of the Closing balance, Total interest, and Closing balance with interest is also provided for each calculation in the report.

If you generate this report in Clio, i.e., you generate a Web report, you have the option to post the calculated interest directly to the client funds you hold. Next to the Total interest amount calculated for the client funds held in a client funds account (per matter and client), click Apply Interest. You can change the transaction date and description for the transaction, then click Record transaction to create this ledger entry in the client funds account. The Source/Destination field for the entry will be “Trust Interest Calculation Report”.

Once you apply interest to the client funds, your subsequent Client funds interest reports will show the last five transactions where you applied interest to the account.

 

Trust management report

The trust management report is designed to give firms an overview of unbilled time and expense activities, trust account balances, and minimum trust thresholds. You can use this report to compare billable work against trust fund holdings. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists the name of each client

Matter

This column lists the matters for each client.

Unbilled amount

This column shows the amount of unbilled time and expense entries for each matter.

Amount in trust

This column shows the amount of funds currently in trust for the client or matter.

Minimum threshold

This column lists the minimum threshold set for matter trust funds. This amount can be changed by editing the matter and changing the number for Trust balance notification under Billing preference.

Amount below minimum

This column shows the amount that a trust balance has fallen below the minimum threshold set for the matter.

 

 

Trust listing report

The trust listing report is designed to give firms a quick summary of client trust fund balances across all client accounts. This report includes an opening and closing balance summary. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Account name

This column shows the name of the trust account.

Last activity date

This column shows the most recent transaction in the client's trust account.

Client balance

This column shows the current amount in trust for the client. This balance may be different from the amount shown in the matter's Dashboard if you generate the report for a specific date range. This means that if a client had trust funds in the account before that selected date range and payments were made during the date range, the report will only pull in transactions, which will result in a negative balance.

Unlinked

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Include balances not associated with a client before running the report. It shows trust funds that are not linked to a specific client.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

 

 

Work in progress report

The work in progress report is designed to give firms a detailed view of unbilled time and expense activities for matters. This report only shows activities on bills in draft, bills pending approval, and activities not on any bills. It will not show activities on any approved or paid bills. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the activity was recorded. Multiple activities with the same date will appear in random order.

User

This column lists the firm user assigned on the activity entry.

Description

This column shows the activity category selected when the activity was created. If no activity category was selected, this column will be blank.

Note

This column shows the description entered when the activity entry was created.

Quantity

This column shows the total number of hours or expenses.

Price

This column shows the selected rate of the listed activities.

Total

This total summarizes the total cost of the time and expense entries. This value may be different from the value under the Price column depending on the Quantity. For example, if the Quantity for an activity is listed as 0.50, the Price is $500, then the Total would be $250

Matter total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for each of the client's matters.

Client total

This total is the summarized total cost of unbilled time and expense entries for all of the client's matters.

 

Bank account activity report

The bank account activity report is designed to give firms a detailed view of funds in and funds out across all firm bank accounts. This report also includes the account balance. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Date

This column shows the date that the transaction occurred in the account. Transactions include deposits, withdrawals, and transfers. Multiple transactions that occur on the same day will appear in random order.

Source/Destination

This column shows the payment type and is gathered from the Source/Destination field from when you are recording a new transaction. If you selected the option to Include opening balance before running the report, this section will first show the opening balance of each trust account, which is helpful if you choose to run the report in a specific date range.

Client

This column lists the client associated with the transaction.

Matter

This column shows the matter that is linked to the transaction.

Description

This column shows the information entered into the Description field when a payment was recorded.

Funds out

This column lists withdrawals or payments from the account, including bank charges.

Funds in

This column lists payments deposited into the account, including interest earned.

Balance

This column shows the amount of money left in the account after each listed transaction.

Closing balance

This lists the closing balance of the Funds out, Funds in, and Balance.

Balance summary

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you selected the option for Display bank account summary before running the report. This section shows the current balance of your accounts. If you sort results by a specific date range, this section will show an opening balance that summarizes the transactions prior to the selected date range and a closing balance that summarizes the account balance at the end of the date range.

Next up

results.name: View Reconciliation Reports
results.title: View Reconciliation Reports
results.body:
Every completed trust account reconciliation produces a report for that reconciliation period. The report is your audit-ready record of the period: it shows the balances you reconciled to, every transaction you matched, and the effect on each client's ledger. You can view the report in Clio Manage or export it as a PDF to use outside Clio.

Note: If your plan includes Clio Accounting, view your reconciliation reports in Clio Accounting instead. See Clio Accounting: Operating and Trust Reconciliation.

What a reconciliation report includes

Each report covers one reconciliation period and is available in three tabs:

  • Reconciliation summary: The ledger and bank account balances for the period, and the difference between them.
  • Transaction details: The transactions for the reconciliation period, broken out as funds in, funds out, bank interest, bank charges, and adjustments. Both cleared and uncleared transactions are included.
  • Client ledger details: The effect of the period's transactions on each client's trust ledger.

Reconciliation reports can be accessed in Clio Manage for 10 years, so you keep a full history for audit and compliance purposes.

 

View a reconciliation report

  1. Go to Accounts.
  2. Click the relevant trust account name.
  3. Select the Reconciliations subtab.
  4. Click View report for the relevant reconciliation.
  5. Use the three tabs to view the reconciliation summary, transaction details, and client ledger details.

 

Export a reconciliation report

Export the report when you need a copy outside Clio Manage, such as for a regulator, an auditor, or your bookkeeper.

  1. Open the reconciliation report using the steps above.
  2. Click Export to download a PDF file of the report.
Tip: The export includes all three tabs, so you do not need to export each one separately.

Up next

  • Void or Delete a Reconciliation: Void a completed reconciliation or delete one that is still in progress.
  • Trust Reconciliation in Clio: Start a reconciliation and match transactions.

results.title: QuickBooks Desktop and Clio
results.body:
QuickBooks desktop is a desktop-based accounting software. You can export payment and trust transactions and bills from Clio to QuickBooks Desktop for accounting purposes.

Tip: Check out the QuickBooks Community Knowledge Base for more information about using QuickBooks, including how to resolve specific error codes.

Set up QuickBooks Desktop

Since QuickBooks Desktop does not integrate directly with Clio, the setup process is done by setting up a Chart of Accounts in QuickBooks Desktop and then mapping Clio IIF exports to QuickBooks ledger accounts. Once this is done, you can begin exporting transactions and bills out of Clio and importing them into QuickBooks Desktop.

Important: Changing the default settings is not recommended unless you are very familiar with QuickBooks Desktop and accounting.
  1. In Clio Manage, go to Accounts > Export transactions.
  2. Under Export Format, click QuickBooks Export Options.
  3. Optional: Change which accounts you want Clio to use with exports.
  4. Click Update QuickBooks Export Options.
  5. To reset the options to default mappings, delete the fields and then click Update QuickBooks Export Options.

 

Export account transactions

You can export account transactions in Clio in either QuickBooks IIF or QuickBooks CSV format. Once exported, go into your QuickBooks Desktop account, and import the file.

  1. Go to Accounts > Export transactions.
  2. Select the bank account you want to export transactions for.
  3. Select the date range for transactions.
  4. Select the QuickBooks export format.
  5. Click Export Transactions.
  6. Import the file into QuickBooks Desktop.

 

Export bills

You can export account transactions in Clio in PDF or CSV format, or as IIF files. Once exported, go into your QuickBooks Desktop account, and import the file.

PDF or CSV IIF
  1. Go to Billing.
  2. Optional: Select the appropriate bill state.
  3. Select the bills you want to export.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Export.
  5. Select the output format.
  6. Click Export.
  7. Import the file into QuickBooks Desktop.
  1. Go to Clio's export page.
  2. Click QuickBooks CSV & IIF next to Bank Transactions or Bills.
  3. Select the relevant export parameters.
  4. Under Format, select Quickbooks IIF.
  5. Click Export Transactions or Export Bills.

 

Perform trust account reconciliation

Tip: Clio offers full trust account reconciliation right in Clio Manage. Learn more here.

If you are performing trust account reconciliation in QuickBooks Desktop, you can do so by exporting trust transactions from Clio to QuickBooks Desktop, running the trust ledger report in Clio, and then matching transactions in QuickBooks Desktop.

  1. Follow the steps above in Export account transactions to export trust transactions and then import them into QuickBooks Desktop.
  2. In Clio Manage, go to Reports > Reports.
  3. Click Client under Categories.
  4. Select the Trust ledger report.
  5. Choose your parameters
  6. Select Generate report.
  7. Go to QuickBooks Desktop and compare the amounts.

results.name: Manage Trust Administration Fee
results.title: Manage Trust Administration Fee
results.body:
The Trust Administration Fee (TAF) is a $20 fee plus 5% GST that the Law Society of British Columbia (LSBC) requires firms to remit for each client matter in which cumulative trust deposits exceed $10,000. It funds the LSBC Trust Assurance Program and is charged once per matter for the life of that matter. Clio Manage can automatically apply this fee, track it across matters, and report it for your quarterly remittance. This article explains how to turn TAF on for your firm, how Clio applies the fee, how to control it per matter, and how to report on it.

Important: The TAF settings are available to accounts with Canada set as the billing country, including firms hosted on US servers. The fee itself is a legal obligation specifically for firms practising in British Columbia under LSBC Rule 2-110.

Understand the fee application

After you enable the setting and apply it to a matter, Clio Manage adds a trust administration fee expense automatically the first time that matter's cumulative trust deposits exceed $10,000, whether the threshold is crossed by a trust deposit or a paid trust bill:

  • The expense is $20, plus 5% GST.
  • It is added once per matter, for the life of the matter, so duplicate charges are not created.
  • It is billable by default and appears on the matter unless you mark the fee as non-billable.

Note: Only trust account transactions created on or after January 1, 2026, count toward the $10,000 threshold, in line with the LSBC transition rule for matters that span the rule change.

 

Enable Trust Administration Fees

Note: Users with Admin, Settings, and Manage Users permissions can enable TAF. 

  1. Click Settings.
  2. Click Firm Preferences.
  3. Click the Compliance tab.
  4. On the Law Society of British Columbia Compliance card, toggle the setting on. The status updates to Trust Administration Fee is enabled, and a 5% GST tax rate is provisioned for the fee.

After you enable the setting, two options are available in the section:

  • Apply to new matters by default: automatically applies the fee to matters created after the setting is enabled. Existing matters are not affected and must be opted in individually.
  • Mark fee as non-billable: records the fee but excludes it from client invoices, so your firm absorbs the cost rather than passing it to the client.

 

Apply or opt out from a matter

Each matter has its own control, so you decide which matters the fee applies to. Enabling the firm setting does not add the fee to existing matters automatically.

Note: The Apply to new matters by default firm option only pre-selects this checkbox on newly created matters. To apply the fee to a matter that already exists, open that matter and select the checkbox.

  1. Create a new matter, or open an existing matter and click Edit.
  2. Go to Billing preferences.
  3. Under Trust administration fee, select Apply a trust administration fee to this matter to apply the fee, or clear it to opt the matter out.
  4. Click Save.

 

Report on the fees applied

The Trust Administration Fees report lists the matters where the fee applies and the amounts, so you can prepare your quarterly remittance to the LSBC.

Note: This is the only report you need from Clio for TAF. You remit the fees to the LSBC through the LSBC online portal each quarter, within 30 days of each quarter-end (March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31).

  1. Click Reports.
  2. Open Classic Reports.
  3. Open the Trust Administration Fees report.
  4. Set the Date range for the period you are filing.
  5. Select the Output format. 
  6. Click Generate report. 

Tip: Under LSBC Rule 2-110, the fee applies separately to each client matter, so a single client with several qualifying matters may owe more than one fee. The fees you collect support the LSBC Trust Assurance Program and are remitted on the schedule set out in Rule 2-111.

 

Up next

  • Trust accounting: see Trust Account Management to manage the trust requests, payments, and balances that determine when the fee applies.
  • Billing the fee: see Generate Bills in Clio Manage to add the trust administration fee expense to a client invoice.

results.title: Clio Manage Reports, Presets, and History
results.body:
In Clio Manage, you can generate reports that provide nuanced insights into your firm’s data. A list of Classic reports are available for you to select then tailor to your needs using filters. If you regularly generate the same report with the same filters applied, you can save this unique combination of report and filters as a “preset”. You can also schedule a report to be automatically generated according to a timeline of your choosing.

For more nuanced reporting needs, Clio Manage also offers the ability to create Custom reports. Refer to Generate Custom Reports in Clio Manage for more information.

 

Generate reports in Clio Manage

Each Clio Manage report has a specific set of filters that apply to that report. You can generate various configurations of each report to suit your reporting needs. You can generate most reports in CSV and PDF format, and some reports can be generated in Excel and Web formats. If you create a report in CSV format, you can also customize how your report appears by hiding, unhiding, and reordering columns.

Important: Restricting the date range for some reports can cause discrepancies between report output data and information in Clio Manage. This is most common when activities are reported in one month and generated on an invoice the following month. Affected reports include the following: revenue, originating attorney revenue, productivity by user, productivity by client, matter productivity by user, and trust listing.
  1. Go to the main Reports tab.
  2. Select the Classic reports tab, and under that, the Reports subtab.
  3. Select a report category under Categories.
  4. Click the name of the report you want to generate.
  5. Select your filter parameters.

  6. Under Output format, select how you want to view the report. If you choose CSV format, click Select and reorder columns to hide, unhide, and/or reorder columns in the report. 

    Select and reorder columns

    You can hide, unhide, and reorder columns for the following Clio Manage reports: Clio Payments ledger report, Clio Payments transaction report, billing rate report, client activity report, fee allocation report, matter balance summary report, matter productivity by user report, originating attorney revenue report, trust ledger report, trust management report, and revenue report.
     

    Note: Hiding a column will not delete any data from the report. Your generated report will not show the column data, but you can always activate the hidden column if you need to see that data.

If you do not want a column to appear in the report, uncheck the box next to a column's name to hide it, or click the three line icon next to a column's name to drag and drop the column under Hidden columns. If you want to reorder the active columns, click the three line icon next to a column's name to drag and drop the column to any position around another active column.
    2. The columns listed under Hidden columns will not appear in the report once the report is generated. If you want to show a hidden column in the report, check the box next to the column's name or click the three line icon next to a column's name and drag and drop it from Hidden columns to Active columns.

Generate, schedule, and manage reports presets

With report presets in Clio Manage, you can quickly generate reports you access on a regular basis. When generating a report, you can save the selected filters as a preset that you can edit at any time, eliminating the need to remember your report filters every time you generate the same report. results.name: Set Up Evergreen Retainers
results.title: Set Up Evergreen Retainers
results.body:
In Clio Manage, evergreen trust is a workflow that automatically replenishes a matter's trust funds. When you enable evergreen trust for a matter, applying trust funds to a bill automatically generates a new trust request whenever the balance drops below the minimum you set. You can also turn on Low balance notification separately to notify firm users, either instead of or alongside the automatic request. This keeps a client's retainer topped up without you having to track the balance or create replenishment requests by hand.

Tip: Learn more about the benefits of evergreen retainers.

Understand evergreen management in Clio Manage

An evergreen retainer follows the same cycle each billing period and enables your firm to automate the trust generation.

Note: If your firm uses Clio Payments, your client can pay a trust request from the request email by card, eCheck, or Pay Later. Otherwise, record the payment yourself after your client pays.

  1. Collect the initial retainer. Create a trust request, send it to your client, and record the payment.
    • See Create Trust Requests and Approve and Send Trust Requests.
  2. Set the minimum trust balance for the matter and turn on evergreen trust.
  3. Record time and expense entries, then generate a bill.
  4. Apply the retained trust funds to the bill.
  5. Review the automatically generated trust request in drafts, approve it, and send it to your client.

 

Set the minimum required amount and enable evergreen trust

The Minimum required amount is the trust balance you want to keep available on the matter. Turning on Enable evergreen trust generates a new trust request automatically whenever you apply trust funds to a bill and the balance drops below this amount. Set the minimum first, then turn on the settings you want. You can turn on evergreen trust and low balance notifications separately.

Note: Evergreen trust applies to trust funds held at the matter level, and cannot generate trust requests for funds held at the client level.

Tip: Each request is created as a draft for your review, and stays in Draft status until a firm member approves and sends it, unless the request is set to skip approval.

Single matter Multiple matters
  1. Go to the matter you want to update, or create a new matter.
  2. Click Edit matter.
  3. Scroll to the Billing preference section, then find Trust balance.
  4. Under Minimum required, enter the trust balance to maintain for this matter.
  5. Turn on Enable evergreen trust.
  6. Optional: Turn on Low balance notification, then under Notify these users, select the firm users to notify.
  7. Click Save matter.
  1. Go to Matters.
  2. Select the checkboxes for the matters you want to update.
  3. Click Edit, then select Update billing preference.
  4. Under Trust balance, enter the Minimum required amount to apply to all selected matters, or leave it blank to keep each matter's current amount.
  5. Under Evergreen trust, select Enabled.
  6. Click Update billing preference.

Note: Bulk edit applies the same minimum required amount to every selected matter. To set a different minimum for an individual matter, edit that matter directly.

 

Monitor trust balances

You can track trust balances on a single matter or across the firm.

On a matter, the Financial section of the matter Dashboard shows the current trust balance, the minimum required amount, and a low-balance indicator once the balance falls below the minimum.

Across the firm, the trust management report shows unbilled activities, trust account balances, and minimum required amounts, so you can compare your billable work against the funds you hold. See Clio Manage Reports, Presets, and History to generate a report, and Clio Manage Client Reports for what the trust management report contains.

 

Apply trust and generate a trust request

Once a minimum required balance is set on an evergreen matter, when you apply trust funds to a bill and the trust balance drops below the required minimum, a trust request automatically generates. When it does, the Evergreen trust section lets you review or update the issue date and due date, add a note, choose whether to skip the approval process, and choose whether to clear the matter's existing trust request.

Important: A generated trust request is a request for funds, not a record of funds received. The matter trust balance does not change until your client pays and you record the payment. See Protect Client Trust Funds.

Understand replenishment calculation

The generated trust request amount is the Minimum required amount minus the matter's current trust balance:

Minimum required − current trust balance = trust request amount

  • A matter with a $2,750.00 minimum, applying trust that brings the balance to $0.00, generates a request for $2,750.00.
  • A matter with a $5,000.00 minimum, applying trust that leaves a $1,000.00 balance, generates a request for $4,000.00.

When Clear old trust requests to prevent duplicates is selected as the default, the new request amount is whichever is higher: the amount needed to reach the minimum, or the amount still owed on the cleared request.

Note: You cannot change the amount of a generated request while applying trust. To choose a different amount, create the trust request yourself and use Autofill.

  1. Generate a bill. See Generate Bills in Bulk, or Generate Quick Bills for a single bill.
  2. Apply trust funds to the bill. See Apply Trust Funds to Bills. You can apply trust to several bills at once from the bills table.
  3. Under Evergreen trust, confirm the number of trust requests to be created, then set the Issue date and Due date.
  4. Optional: Click Add note to add a note to the request.
  5. Optional: Select Skip the trust request approval process to send the request without approval from another firm member.

  6. Review Clear old trust requests to prevent duplicates, then confirm to apply the trust funds.

    Important: Clear old trust requests to prevent duplicates is selected by default. Clearing deletes draft requests, voids unpaid requests, and writes off the remaining balance on partially paid requests. Clear the checkbox to keep existing requests. When a partial payment is still pending, write off the remaining amount yourself after the payment completes.

  7. Review the request and send it to your client to collect the funds. See Approve and Send Trust Requests.

 

Replenish manually with Autofill

If you have enabled evergreen trust on a matter and need to manually top up the matter, you can create a trust request and use Autofill to calculate the replenishment amount. 

  1. In Clio Manage, go to the matter Dashboard.
  2. In the Financial section, under Matter trust funds, click New request.
  3. Confirm the Issue date, Due date, Client, and Matter, and set Balance type to Matter.

  4. Open the Autofill menu beside the Amount label and choose an option. Each option shows its calculated amount, so you can compare them before you choose.

    Note: The four options show the same amount when a matter has no outstanding balance and no unbilled work in progress. Replenish uses the same target as evergreen trust: the matter's Minimum required trust balance.

    • Replenish: Bring the matter trust balance back up to the minimum required.
    • Replenish + outstanding balance: The replenishment amount plus any outstanding balance on the client's bills.
    • Replenish + WIP: The replenishment amount plus unbilled work in progress.
    • Replenish + outstanding balance + WIP: The replenishment amount plus outstanding balances and unbilled work in progress.
  5. Optional: Edit the Amount field to override the calculated amount.
  6. Click Save trust request.

 

Up next

  • Create Trust Requests: Create a trust request and use Autofill to calculate the amount.
  • Approve and Send Trust Requests: Approve a generated request and send it to your client.
  • Record Payments on Trust Requests: Record your client's trust deposit against the request.

You can export your firm's data from Clio Manage for record-keeping or to migrate data to a new Clio Manage account. Exported files are downloaded in CSV format and can be used with Clio's migration templates to import data into another account.

Note: Only users with administrator permissions can export data in bulk.

Export data from Clio Manage

  1. In Clio Manage, go to the Exports page:
    • North America: https://app.clio.com/export

  2. Click Excel ready CSV next to each of the following data types you want to export:

  3. To export outstanding balances, go to Reports, click Reports, then click Accounts receivable. Set the output format to CSV and click Generate Report.

 

Migrate data to a new Clio Manage account

results.name: Prepare Data For Migration
results.title: Prepare Data For Migration
results.body:
Reviewing and cleaning your data before migration ensures that records transfer accurately into Clio Manage. Clio's migrations team does not clean or modify your data. Any errors or duplicates in your previous system will carry over on import.

Important: Set a firm-wide cut-off time before your scheduled export. Once you export data from your previous system, stop using it immediately. Any data entered after the export will not be captured in Clio Manage. You will need to manually transfer the data entered after the export. Do not enable contact or calendar syncs, or any Clio integrations, until your migration is complete.

Contacts

Verify that data appears in the correct column before exporting. Phone numbers should not appear in email fields, and company names should not appear in name fields. Check a sample of records, including the first and last rows, to confirm data is correctly placed. Include the following fields.

  • First name
  • Last name
  • Company name (required for company contacts)

 

Matters

Matters without a description will be assigned a placeholder description on import. Matters without an assigned client will be assigned to an unknown client. Include the following fields.

  • Matter status (Open, Pending, or Closed)
  • Matter custom number
  • Matter description
  • Client

 

Activities

Time entries without an assigned user will not import. If you need to import data for a user who will not be added to the Clio account, contact your migrations representative. Include the following fields.

  • Date
  • Quantity
  • Rate
  • User

 

Calendar events

Verify that your calendar events have exported correctly by checking a sample of past and future events, including court dates and scheduled meetings. Include the following fields.

  • Calendar summary
  • Start date and start time
  • End date and end time
  • Destination or user calendar

 

Contact and matter notes

Contact notes will not import without a contact or company name. Matter notes will not import without a matter number. Include the following fields.

Contact notes

Date, subject, note description, and first name, last name, or company name.

Matter notes

Date, subject, note description, and matter number.

 

Related contacts

Each related contact requires a matter. Include the following fields.

  • Matter
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Company name

 

Tasks

Tasks without an assigned user will not import. If your tasks do not have an assigned user, remove them from the data set or confirm with your migrations representative. Include the following fields.

  • Status (Pending, In-Progress, or Complete)
  • Task name
  • Due date
  • Assigned user

 

Accounts receivable balances

Verify that the balances exported from your previous system are correct before submitting. If your export includes multiple columns with outstanding amounts, identify which amount should be imported and confirm this with your migrations representative. Include the following fields.

  • Balance
  • User
  • Date

 

Manage the firm during the transition period

Data processing typically takes several business days, depending on the size and complexity of your data. During this period, your firm will need to continue recording time and expenses in Clio Manage. Records added during the transition period will need to be reconciled after migration is complete.

Use one of the following methods to track activities during the transition period.

Method 1: Placeholder matter

Create a temporary matter to record time entries while waiting for the migration to complete. Once migration is confirmed accurate, an administrator can move the time entries in bulk to their respective matters.

  1. In Clio Manage, click Contacts.
  2. Create a new company contact using your firm's name.
  3. Create a new matter for this contact and enter Placeholder - Migrations as the matter description.
  4. Add time entries to this matter, using the Description field to specify which matter each entry belongs to.
  5. Once migration is complete and data accuracy is confirmed, move the time entries in bulk to their respective matters.

 

Method 2: Import templates

You can track activities and matter notes using Clio's migration import templates, then upload the completed spreadsheet into Clio Manage and link entries to their respective matters after migration. See Get Started with Migration Templates for template downloads and import instructions.

Note: Generate bills for any outstanding time and expense entries in your previous software before the cut-off date to obtain the most current outstanding balances. Apply credits and trust payments to outstanding bills before exporting, as credits and trust balances will not be migrated. Export any historical banking and trust reports you want to retain as reference documents and upload them to Clio Manage under the Documents tab.

 

Up Next

Once migration is complete, review Manage Clio Manage Data After Migration for steps to verify your imported data and process outstanding accounts receivable balances.

results.name: Multi-Client Matters in Clio Manage and Clio Grow
results.title: Multi-Client Matters in Clio Manage and Clio Grow
results.body:
With Multi-Client Matters (MCM), you can now add multiple clients to a single matter. This feature eliminates the need for manual workarounds—like duplicate matters or combined contact names—allowing you to manage complex cases with greater accuracy and professionalism.

Note: This feature is available to select plans. Learn more about your plan's features. If you need to upgrade your firm’s plan, ask a firm administrator.

Add multiple clients to matters

You can add up to 11 clients to a matter when creating or editing a matter in Clio Manage. Adding multiple clients to your matter allows you to accurately manage the contacts on a matter who are employing your firm, whereas you can then use related contacts exclusively for entities connected to the matter but not represented by your firm (e.g., opposing counsel, witnesses, etc.).

When adding multiple clients to a matter, you can select which client to make the “default client”. Certain functionality in Clio Manage applies to this single default client (e.g., some reports apply to the default client only).

  • Searchability: Searching for a client via Global Search will show the contact and all matters the client has been added to.

 

Joint billing

Adding multiple clients to a matter allows you to generate invoices that include the names of all of those clients, removing the need to manually edit bills with external tools. When adding a client, you can choose whether they should be a bill recipient, which determines whether they receive a copy of the bill.

Joint billing is therefore suited to situations where all clients are jointly liable for the bill. You can continue using split billing if clients need separate invoices for their portion of the bill.

To generate a new joint bill, go to Billing, then click New bills. Multi-Client Matters does not currently support generating Quick Bills. 
 

Multi-Client trust accounting

Trust funds received from any client added to a matter can be deposited and held at the matter level. The record will log which client paid the funds.

When applying available trust funds to a bill, you will need to select the client whose trust funds you would like to apply to the bill. Currently, Clio does not allow you to specify an order or draw from multiple clients in a single transaction.

 

Trust account reports

The following reports support multi-client trust accounting:

  • Matter balance summary
  • Trust management
  • Invoice payments 
  • Client Ledger
  • Trust Listing 

All other reports will continue to apply only to the default client.

 

Client portals

When you create a new client portal for a matter with multiple clients, Clio will add all clients to the portal. This ensures every client has access to communications, updates, and documents.

If the client portal was created before adding additional clients to a matter, you will need to manually add those clients to the portal.

 

Document templates

You can use the <<Matter.AllClients.Names>> merge field when creating any document templates to automatically populate the names of all clients added to the matter. When you generate a document using your template for a matter with multiple clients, you will be able to select which client's information to populate in the relevant document fields. If you do not select a specific client, the information for the matter’s default client will be used.

 

Convert multi-contact matter in Clio Grow to multi-client matter in Clio Manage

You can now select which contact added to matter in Clio Grow to set as the default client and which contacts to add as additional clients on the matter. When the matter is converted to Clio Manage, these selections carry over with those contacts not  selected as clients being added as related contacts.

To indicate which contacts to add as clients to the matter in Clio Matter:

  1. Open a matter in Clio Grow and click Edit Matter.
  2. In the Contacts section, use the Set as default client radio button to select the default client.
  3. For each contact you want to add as a client to the matter, check the checkbox for This contact is a client below the contact’s name.
  4. Click Save.

When viewing the matter page, contacts marked as clients will have display a Client label.

When converting a matter from Clio Grow to Clio Manage, in the Related Contacts section of the conversion modal, contacts you previously selected as clients will have the checkbox for This contact is a client preselected. You can make adjustments before converting the matter.

results.name: Accounting Reports
results.title: Accounting Reports
results.body:
Clio Accounting reports provide a detailed overview of your firm's accounting processes. Regularly generating these reports can help you get a good understanding of your firm's financial situation, spot discrepancies, and remain compliant. If your firm is required to submit regular trust reconciliation reports to state bar associations or your law society, staying on top of your reconciliations and reports can make it easier to make those submissions.

 

Generate reports

Depending on your law firm, you may access reports at the end of each month, gearing up for the end of a month, or at another period in the month. It may be most beneficial to generate accounting reports after doing bank feed matching and account reconciliation, allowing you to compare your report results to your reconciled accounts.

Note: Reconciliation reports are only available once an account reconciliation is completed. Learn more about operating and trust account reconciliation and how to view reconciliation reports.

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. Select the name of a report you want to generate.
  3. Fill in the relevant details. Each report requires you to fill a set of fields relevant to that report.
    • Reporting period or a custom Start date and End date: Select an option from the Reporting period menu, or use the Start date and End date to select a custom date range.
    • As of date: Select the calendar date for which you want to generate a snapshot of your firm's financial position at the close of that business day.
    • Accounting method: Select Accrual basis if you want the report to show transactions at the time that revenue is earned and expenses incurred, or select Cash basis if you want the report to show transactions according to when funds change hands.
    • Only show accounts with balances: Check this box to exclude accounts with no balance.
    • Ledger accounts: When generating a General ledger report, you can select a specific ledger, or generate the report for all ledgers.
    • Output to: Select Web to view the report in Clio, or select PDF or CSV to download a copy of the report to your computer in either of these formats.

 

Profit and loss statement

The profit and loss statement provides a breakdown of revenues and expenses that make up your net income. You can generate this report at any time, but reviewing it on a monthly basis helps ensure accurate financial reporting.

Note: For payment allocations, partial payments on bills are distributed equally across income and expense categories.

The profit and loss statement organizes transactions into revenue and expense categories based on your Chart of Accounts. These categories may include:

  • Revenue: Client refunds, fee income, interest income, service income, uncategorized income.
  • Expenses: Operating expenses such as processing fees and payroll.

Summary amounts are underlined and you can click these amounts to view the individual transactions behind it.

 

General ledger report

The general ledger report shows all financial activity transactions for your firm in a specific period of time. It includes general ledger account names, beginning balances, payments, interest, dates, and totals for each account. Summary amounts are underlined and you can click these amounts to view the individual transactions behind it.

 

Balance sheet report

The balance sheet report informs on what you own (assets) and owe (liabilities) within a certain period of time. It shows current and long-term assets, current and long-term liabilities, shareholders' equity, and current debt and equity ratios. This report will not show account receivables, trust accounts, or undeposited funds accounts. This report should be generated monthly. Summary amounts are underlined and you can click these amounts to view the individual transactions behind it.

 

Trial balance report

The trial balance report lists the ending balances of all general ledger accounts, including the total of each asset, liability, equity, expense, and income account. It can help you identify the balance of debit and credit entries from the transactions recorded in the general ledger at a certain point in time. This report should be generated monthly before generating the balance sheet report. Summary amounts are underlined and you can click these amounts to view the individual transactions behind it.

 

Cash flow statement report

The cash flow statement shows your firm's incoming and outgoing cash at a given time. It measures your firm's strength, profitability, and long-term future outlook. This report can help you determine whether your firm has enough liquidity or cash to pay its expenses and can predict future cash flow to help you with budgeting your matters. This report will not show account receivables and account payable funds. This report should be generated monthly. Summary amounts are underlined and you can click these amounts to view the individual transactions behind it.

 

Reconciliation report

Reconciliation reports provide a summary and details overview of completed operating and trust account reconciliations. For trust account reconciliations, you can view a summary of cleared and uncleared balance in client ledger accounts and easily provide details that trace back the source of each transaction if your firm is audited.

Once generated, you can view and print the Reconciliation report as a PDF.

 

Vendor expenses report

The vendor expenses report shows your firm's operating expenses grouped by vendor. For each vendor, the report lists individual transactions including the transaction date, category, payment method, account, description, and amount, along with a total for each vendor.

 

Tax summary report

Available to users in Canada, the tax summary report shows the sales tax your firm collected and the input tax credits it can claim for a period, organized by the line numbers used on a sales tax return. You can use it to transfer your figures onto your return, and to see exactly which transactions make up each amount.

Generate this report for each tax authority you report to by selecting the authority from the Tax authority menu.

At the top of the report, three totals summarize the period: 

  • Total tax collected: The sales tax your firm charged on its billing.
  • Total ITC credits: The tax your firm paid on its purchases and can claim back.
  • Net tax owing: The amount owing to the tax authority, calculated as tax collected minus your credits and adjustments. 

Below the totals, the report lists each line with its line number.

Important: Review these figures against your own records before you file. If you are unsure whether an amount belongs on your return, check with your accountant or bookkeeper.
Tip: The amounts in the report are clickable links that allow you to open a transaction detail report listing each transaction and relevant transaction details behind the figure.

Once generated, you can export the transaction detail report to CSV.

results.body:
Clio's Trust Center publishes Clio's security and compliance posture for each Clio product. Your firm can review public security information without an account, and request access to audit reports, certifications, and policies for a vendor security assessment. The documents support your firm's own security review and vendor approval process.

Note: Clio is unable to provide regulatory or legal advice. Consult your compliance team or legal counsel to confirm whether a Clio product meets your firm's specific regulatory requirements.

Select a Clio product

The Trust Center holds a separate page for each Clio product group. Certification coverage, audit report types, and subprocessors differ between those pages, so the product selection determines which documents a request returns.

  1. Go to trust.clio.com.
  2. Select your firm's product from the dropdown in the top right. The Clio page covers Clio Manage and Clio Grow.

Important: Certifications, audit report types, and subprocessors differ between the three product pages. Confirm the product selection before relying on any document.

 

Request access to security documents

You will need to request access to documents with a lock icon. Documents without a lock icon are public. Locked documents (e.g., audit reports, policies, insurance certificates, and self-assessments) require an access request and a non-disclosure agreement. Clio's Compliance team reviews each request on business days. Requests submitted over a weekend are reviewed the following business day.

  1. Go to Documents.
  2. Click Get access.
  3. Complete the request form and accept the non-disclosure agreement. Use the email linked to your Clio account. Requests from personal emails are denied without review. 

 

Find and download documents

Approved documents open from the same product page used for the request. The Documents section groups documents by category, and the All, Public, and Private filters narrow the list. Search content finds a document by name. Some reports are published as summaries rather than in full, such as the Pentest Report Summary.

  1. Open a document to download it.
  2. To retrieve several documents at once, click Bulk download.

Tip: To receive notice of each new audit report, click Subscribe in the Trust Center Updates section.

 

Up next

Compliance: Review Clio's security protection mechanisms, regional regulatory information, and data residency options.
