results.body:
Reconciliation is the process of comparing records to identify any discrepancies between them and check that your firm's records are correct. When there are no unexplained differences, the record is reconciled. Reconciliation is a key part of preventing fraud and maintaining regulatory compliance, and should be performed on a regular basis depending on your jurisdiction. Reconciling your bank accounts is a critical part of compliance that all firms need to do. If your firm maintains and uses trust accounts, trust account reconciliation is equally, if not more so, important.

 

Operating account reconciliation

In Clio Accounting, operating accounts undergo two-way reconciliation, where you compare bank records to corresponding ledger accounts (client transactions grouped by each client). When there are no unexplained differences, the record is reconciled. Once reconciled, you can view summary reports or void reconciliations.

Note: You should reconcile your operating accounts after doing bank feed matching and ensuring that all transactions on your bank statement have corresponding records in Clio Accounting.

Tip: Reconciling your accounts monthly is recommended. Depending on your jurisdiction, you may need to reconcile accounts monthly or quarterly, but checking more often is recommended—this way, you have less transactions to check at one time, making it easier to spot errors. Doing regular bank reconciliations can also help you catch fraud and errors early on and within enough time for recourse.

Reconcile operating account
  1. Go to Banking and click the three vertical dots (more icon) for the account you would like to reconcile. Select Reconcile now. Alternatively, you can go to Chart of accounts, select the name of the bank account, and click Reconcile.

  2. Complete the details depending on whether this is your first reconciliation in Clio Accounting or a subsequent reconciliation.

    Tip: You can align your reconciliation periods with your bank statement(s) to simplify the process
    • First reconciliation: Enter the Start date and Start balance from your statement. The End date is the last day of the reconciliation period, and the End balance is the balance on the end date. Refer to your statement for the End date and End balance.

    • Subsequent reconciliation: The Start date is automatically set to the day after your last reconciliation's End date, and the Start balance is automatically set to the end balance from the previous reconciliation. Enter the End date as the last day of the current reconciliation period, and the End balance as the balance on the end date. Refer to your bank statement for the End date and End balance.

      Note: If you already started a reconciliation that you’ve not completed, you will be notified and redirected to the Chart of accounts. Click Continue reconciliation for the relevant account.
  3. Review the three sections at the top and the table at the bottom to check if your accounts balance.
    • Bank records: This shows the information you provided in the previous step. The Bank ending balance should match the Clio ending balance in the Clio Accounting records section.
    • Clio Accounting records: This shows the records in Clio Accounting. The account is reconciled when the Clio ending balance matches the Bank ending balance in the Bank records section.
    • Difference: This section will show the difference between the ending balances for your bank records and Clio Accounting records. The ending balances will need to be $0 to reconcile the account.
    • Clio Accounting records table: This table shows individual records that you check or uncheck to include or exclude for the reconciliation period.
      • Exclude (uncheck) transactions that do not have a corresponding entry in your bank account statement.
      • As you check and/or uncheck transactions, the amount for the difference will update accordingly.

  4. When the difference is $0, click Finish.

    • If there are any uncleared transactions that you did not include in your reconciliation, a modal with a list of these transactions will appear. The list of uncleared transactions should include only those transactions that have been recorded in Clio Manage but that have not yet cleared through the bank (e.g., a check deposited on October 31st may not appear on the October bank statement since it can take a few of days for the deposit to be processed). Any other transactions should be reconciled before finishing the reconciliation. If there are no items on this list that should not appear, click Finish.


    The reconciliation report shows a summary of ledger and account balances, cleared transactions and uncleared transactions, and bank charges and bank interest. You can click Choose Files in this section to upload a copy of the relevant bank statement(s).

    • Cleared transactions: This section shows some of the individual funds in and funds out transactions in Clio Accounting that also appeared and matched on the bank statement.
    • Uncleared transactions: This section shows some of the details of individual funds in and funds out transactions recorded in Clio Accounting that have not yet cleared through the bank. If you have uncleared transactions in this reconciliation period, you would want to review them in the next period.
  5. Optional: Click the Details tab to see a comprehensive list of every transaction included in the reconciliation.
  6. Optional: To save a digital copy of the reconciliation summary or details on your computer, click Print to PDF from the relevant tab. If you need a physical copy, you can print the downloaded PDF.
  7. Optional: If you need to make any changes to the reconciliation, click Void. Voiding will delete the reconciliation, which means you will need to start from the beginning again.
View reconciliation report
  1. Go to Reports and select Reconciliation.
  2. For the reconciliation that you want to view, click View to open the report.
Void reconciliation
  1. Go to Reports and select Reconciliation.
  2. For the reconciliation that you want to void, click View to open the report.
  3. Click Void, then confirm the action by clicking Void again.

The voided reconciliation will still appear in the list of reconciliation reports, but you will not be able to view the voided report. When you void a reconciliation, the action is permanent. However, once voided, you can simply redo the reconciliation while correcting any previous errors you may have made.

Note: Completed reconciliations are locked to protect the integrity of your trust account. If you need to make a correction to a previously reconciled period, such as editing or deleting a transaction, you will have to void the reconciliation and then redo it.

Each new reconciliation for a bank account uses information from the previous reconciliation—specifically the end date and end balance for the previous reconciliation is used to inform the start date and start balance of the new reconciliation. For this reason you will be unable to void a reconciliation for a particular bank account if there are newer reconciliations. If you do need to void a reconciliation for a particular time period, you will first need to void all reconciliations for more recent time periods.

 

Trust account reconciliation

In Clio Accounting, trust accounts undergo three-way reconciliation, where you compare three financial records to ensure they correspond with one another. These three records are the trust account's bank records, the client trust ledger containing all transaction entries related to a specific client, and the firm's trust ledger containing all trust transactions. When all three records align and there are no unexplained differences, the account is reconciled. In Clio Accounting, you can view summary reports of previous reconciliations or void reconciliations, if necessary.

There are two options for backing up Juris data. See the steps below for more information.

  • Juris Management Console Backup
  • Backing up Juris using SQL Server management Studio

Note: All users will need to be logged out of Juris for the backup.

Option 1: Juris Management Console Backup

Juris backups include Juris Suite time and expense entries that have been synchronized with the server, as indicated with an entry key within the grid. Time and expense entries stored only in the local cache file (not synchronized) are not included in the backup. Additionally, backing up via Juris Management Console also shrinks the LDF file upon completion. Follow these steps to create a backup using the Juris Management Console (JMC):

  1. Verify that all users have closed Juris.
  2. Click the Start button on the Windows Taskbar.
  3. Select Programs > Juris > Administrative Tools > Juris Management Console to the open the Juris Management Console window.
  4. Double-click Juris Management Console to expand the folder in the Juris Console list.
  5. Double-click [Your Firms Name] Data to expand the folder.
  6. Right-click the Database folder and select All Tasks and then Backup to open the Juris Backup wizard.
  7. Click the Right Arrow button once.
  8. Select New Backup from the Backup Device list.
  9. Enter the Name of your backup in the Name field. For example you can enter Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or End of year as the name of your backup file.
  10. Click to check the File radial box to enter a destination path for saving your backup.
  11. Click the ellipsis button to open the Browse for location of Backup file window.
  12. Select the folder you want to save your backup to. The file path needs to reside on the server and not on the local workstation.
  13. Click OK to return to the Add New Backup Device window.
  14. Enter \[Name of your backup].bak at the end of the destination path in the File field. The [Name of your backup] is the same name as you entered for step 9.
  15. Click OK.
  16. Click the Right Arrow button once.
  17. Click the Right Arrow button to open the Backup Confirmation window and do not change the Media Name field. The Media Name field is populated from the Windows System Clock.
  18. Click Finish to backup Juris.
  19. Click the X to close the Juris Management Console.

 

Option 2: Backing up Juris using SQL Server management Studio

Follow these steps to backup your Juris data using the SQL Server Management Studio:

  1. Verify that all users have closed the Juris program.
  2. Place Juris in Maintenance or Backup mode depending on reason for backup.
  3. Click Start and select Programs > Microsoft SQL Server > SQL Server Management Studio to the open the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio window.
  4. Log in with your credentials.
  5. Click next to Databases to expand it.
  6. Right-click Juris [ your client code ] and select Tasks, and then Back Up... to open the Back Up Database - Juris[ your client code ]window.
  7. Select Full from the Backup type: dropdown list.
  8. Enter the[ Name of your backup ] in the Name field.
  9. Click Add... to open the Select Backup Destination window.
  10. Click the ellipsis button to the right of the File name field to open the Locate Database Files window.
  11. Click to select the folder where you want to save your backup.
  12. Enter the[ Name of your backup ].bak in the File name field and click OK.
  13. Click OK on the Select Backup Destination window.
  14. Click OK on the Back Up Database - Juris [ your client code ] window to start the backup.
  15. Click OK on the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio The backup of database 'Juris[ your client code ]' completed successfully window.
  16. Right-click JBills[ your client code ] and select Tasks, and then Back Up... to open the Back Up Database - JBills[ your client code ] window.
  17. Select Full from the Backup type dropdown list.
  18. Enter the [ name of your backup ] in the Name field. Use the same Backup set Name that you used for Juris[ your client code ]to append the JBills database backup to the Juris database backup.
  19. Click Add... to open the Select Backup Destination window.
  20. Click the ellipsis button to the right of the File name field to open the Locate Database Files window.
  21. Click to select the folder where you want to save your backup. Use the same destination file that you used forJuris[ your client code ]to append the JBills database backup to the Juris database backup.
  22. Enter the name of your backup in the File name field and click OK. Use the same File name that you used forJuris[ your client code ]to append the JBills database backup to the Juris database backup.
  23. Click OK on the Select Backup Destination window.
  24. Click OK on the Back Up Database - JBills[ your client code ] window to start the backup.
  25. Click OK on the Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio The backup of database 'JBills[ your client code ]' completed successfully window.
  26. Close Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio.

QuickBooks Online is cloud-based accounting software. With Clio’s integration with QuickBooks Online, you can sync your Clio contacts, approved bills, trust transactions, payment transactions, and expenses for accounting purposes. You can also print checks.

Important: Check with your accountant or Clio Certified Consultant for which settings are best for your firm. You can search for a Clio Certified Consultant here.
Tip: Take a look at the QuickBooks Community Knowledge Base for more information about using QuickBooks, including how to resolve QuickBooks error codes.

Integration at a glance

Clio's integration with QuickBooks Online allows you to integrate your key processes in Clio Manage with QuickBooks Online. At a high-level, in Clio Manage, you can manage tasks and calendars, store documents, generate and share client bills, track communications, and remind clients of outstanding balances. In QuickBooks Online, you can manage the general ledger, pay operating expenses, reconcile accounts, cut checks for other expenses, and manage tax forms. 

Note: Clio syncs at the account level, not to sub-accounts within Quickbooks.

How key data flows between Clio Manage and QuickBooks Online

  1. In Clio Manage, add a contact.
    • Contacts are synced to QuickBooks Online once contacts have approved bills in Clio. Updates are bi-directional. 
  2. In Clio Manage, add funds to a trust account.
    • Trust funds are added in QuickBooks Online.
  3. In QuickBooks Online, cut a check to a vendor for reimbursable client expenses. 
    • Import into Clio as hard costs and then enter time and other expenses in Clio Manage.
  4. In Clio Manage, draft a bill.
  5. In Clio Manage, approve the bill.
    • The bill is synced to QuickBooks Online.
  6. In Clio Manage, edit the bill invoice.
    • The bill invoice is edited in QuickBooks Online.
  7. In Clio Manage, pay the bill.
    • The bill is paid QuickBooks Online.
  8. In Clio Manage, disburse remaining trust funds.
    • Print a check in QuickBooks Online.

 

Set up integration

Note: You can only set up the Clio integration with QuickBooks Online if you have a QuickBooks online subscription and account. Clio integrates with QuickBooks Online Essentials, Plus, and Accountant (Advanced) but does not support the timekeeper or import hard costs features with QuickBooks Online Essentials. Clio does not integrate with QuickBooks Online Self-Employed (Simple Start).

Important: Before starting, ensure that your contact first name, last name, and email match between Clio and Quickbooks to prevent duplicate contacts from being created.

Step 1: Set up Chart of Accounts in QuickBooks Online

  1. Go to QuickBooks Online.
  2. Set up your accounting ledgers in your Chart of Accounts.

 

Step 2: Configure suggested settings in QuickBooks Online

Before linking your QuickBooks Online account to Clio, you need to enable two settings to establish a proper sync connection and to prevent duplication of bill numbers.

  1. Go to QuickBooks Online.
  2. Click the gear icon to open your settings and then select Account and Settings.
  3. Select the Sales subtab.
  4. Click the pencil icon to edit Sales form content.
  5. Check the box next to Custom Transaction Numbers.
  6. Click Save.
  7. Select the Advanced subtab.
  8. Click the pencil icon to edit Other preferences.
  9. Check the box beside Warn me when I enter a bill number that's already been used for that supplier.
  10. Click Save.

Note: If you are starting in QuickBooks Online before Clio, adjust your first bill number in Clio to be a higher number than the last bill in QuickBooks Online. This will avoid duplication error since both Clio and QuickBooks Online will automatically number your first bill as number one.

 

Step 3: Link Clio to QuickBooks Online

You can link your Clio account to your QuickBooks Online account in your Clio Manage settings.

  1. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  2. Click Connect to QuickBooks.
  3. Click Connect to grant Clio access to your QuickBooks Online account.
  4. Log in to QuickBooks Online and authorize the integration.

Sync trust transactions and enable check printing

In the integration's settings, you can enable the trust transactions and check printing sync. This means that trust transactions recorded in Clio, including trust deposits, disbursements, and applied trust funds, will be exported to QuickBooks Online as journal entries in the Trust Liabilities Account. Clio contacts with trust transactions will also be synced to QuickBooks Online. You can also schedule checks to be printed. Once printed, QuickBooks Online will send check numbers back to Clio.

Note: You can sync up to 15 trust accounts from Clio to QuickBooks Online.

  1. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  2. Beside QuickBooks Online click Configure Settings.
  3. Check the box for Export trust transactions and check printing.
  4. Select the Clio trust account you want to sync to QuickBooks Online.
  5. Select the QuickBooks Online trust bank account and trust liability account you want to sync with Clio.
  6. Enter the start date for sync. Clio will only sync trust transactions from on or after this date.
  7. Optional: Check the box for Trust Disbursement & Check Printing to enable check printing.
  8. Click Save sync settings.

  

 

Import hard costs

Note: This feature is available to select plans. Learn more about your plan's features. If you need to upgrade your firm’s plan, ask a firm administrator.

When configuring the integration’s settings in Clio, you can enable importing hard costs into Clio. This means that all hard cost expenses recorded in QuickBooks Online will be exported back to Clio. This is the only integration feature that syncs data from QuickBooks Online to Clio. Additionally, Clio contacts with active matters will also be synced to QuickBooks Online.

Important: To use this feature, you are required to enable hard and soft costs expenses in your Clio Manage bill settings. Learn more about how to do this here.
Note: Only Expense and Check transaction types from QuickBooks Online will be imported into Clio.

Step 1: Turn on the "track by customer" setting in QuickBooks Online

  1. Click the settings gear icon and select Account and Settings.
  2. Select Expenses.
  3. Click the Bills and expenses area and then turn on Track expenses and items by customer.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Done.

 

Step 2: Enable the feature in Clio Manage

The user assigned to the expense entry in Clio automatically defaults to the primary subscriber. The expense entry can be edited in Clio to change the user. 

  1. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  2. Beside QuickBooks Online click Configure Settings.
  3. Check the box for Import hard costs.
  4. Enter the date you want to start importing hard costs.
    • The contact associated with the hard cost must also have a matter created in Clio.
    • You can always change the date after the initial setup if you want to import from a different date. 
  5. Select the QuickBooks Online ledger from which Clio should import hard costs.
  6. Click Save sync settings.

Only Expense and Check transaction types from QuickBooks Online will be imported into Clio. When creating an expense or check in QuickBooks Online, ensure that the category you select in QuickBooks Online matches the one you selected in Clio Manage within Category Details (e.g. Reimbursable Expenses).

Revoke access to QuickBooks Online

If you disconnect Clio's access to your QuickBooks Online account, the sync still maintains a memory of links between your synced bills, contacts, and payments in case you want to reauthorize access at a later time. If you connect to a different QuickBooks Online account after disconnecting the original account, you will lose the memory of links with the original QuickBooks Online account.

  1. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  2. Beside QuickBooks Online click Configure Settings.
  3. Click Disconnect from QuickBooks Online.

 

Choose how taxes appear in QuickBooks Online

When you enable the sync for approved bills and recorded payments, Line Item Tax Options controls how tax from a Clio Manage bill appears on the synced invoice in QuickBooks Online.

  • Send line item taxes as their own distinct line item: Clio will create a separate line item for the tax amount for each individual time entry or expense. This option will not show a summary of total taxes.
  • Aggregate line item taxes into a single line item: Clio will create a single line item to sum up the total amount for each type of tax. This option will not show a summary of total taxes.
  • Include tax with corresponding line item: Clio will integrate with QuickBooks Online's tax centre, which means that Clio will import sales tax rates from QuickBooks Online to perform sales tax calculations. If you select this option, Clio will override the primary and secondary tax values in your Bill Settings with values specified in QuickBooks Online. This option is only available for non-US versions of QuickBooks Online and will only apply to new bills created after enabling the feature.
Note: QuickBooks Online does not permit two separate taxes on the same line item. If your firm charges two taxes, combine them into a single Group Tax in QuickBooks Online.

 

Troubleshoot QuickBooks Online error codes

If you are experiencing syncing errors and discrepancies between Clio and QuickBooks Online, see below for a list of error codes and resolutions. If you are still having trouble resolving any issues after following the directions below, contact Clio's support team for additional assistance.

(120)

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • This error occurs when the user who initially set up the Clio to QuickBooks Online sync is disabled in QuickBooks Online. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. In Clio Manage, go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  2. Click Configure next to QuickBooks Online.
  3. Click Disconnect from QuickBooks Online.
  4. Click Connect to set up the sync with an enabled user.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (403)

(403)

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • Incorrect Local Area Network (LAN) settings when accessing a web page. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Remove the specified proxy from your web browser.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (503)

(503)

This error code can be caused by the following situation:

  • This is a general error that usually means that QuickBooks Online is having server issues. The error will go away on its own once QuickBooks Online has resolved the issues they are having. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. If there is another error code, review the resolution for that error code to solve the error.
  2. Give QuickBooks Online time to resolve any server issues or reach out to them directly.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (610)

(610)

This error code can be caused by the following situation:

  • The item was deleted in either QuickBooks Online or Clio. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Void the bill.
  2. Generate a new bill and re-apply payment.
  3. Wait for the bill to sync to QuickBooks Online.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (620)

(620)

This error code can be caused by any of the following situations:

  • A bill or sales receipt record with this number already exists in QuickBooks Online.
  • This bill or sales receipt in QuickBooks Online exists under a different customer than the customer for the bill in Clio.
  • The existing bill or sales receipt record in QuickBooks Online is a different or unrelated record. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. If the matter or client was modified after the bill was synced to QuickBooks Online, revert the changes.
  2. Change the bill invoice ID to a unique value and then re-sync.
  3. Regenerate the bill to force the re-sync with a new transaction ID.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (2020)

(2020)

This error code can be caused by one of the following situations:

  • QuickBooks Online Error Code (2020): Invalid Line. Required parameter Line is missing in the request: Bills may not have any line items with monetary value.
  • QuickBooks Online Error Code (2020): Invalid DepositToAccountRef. Required parameter DepositToAccountRef is missing in the request: The Undeposited Funds account is not mapped correctly. 

To resolve "QuickBooks Online Error Code (2020): Invalid Line. Required parameter Line is missing in the request," follow these steps:

  1. Include line items to the bill or remove the bill from Clio.

 

To resolve "QuickBooks Online Error Code (2020): Invalid DepositToAccountRef. Required parameter DepositToAccountRef is missing in the request," follow these steps:

  1. Confirm that an Undeposited Funds account exists in the connected QuickBooks Online account.
    • In QuickBooks Online, click the gear icon and select Chart of Accounts. 
      • Account Type = Other Current Assets
      • Detail Type = Undeposited Funds
      • Name = Undeposited Funds
      • It is not a sub-account
    • Click Save and Close.
  2. In Clio Manage, go to the QuickBooks Online sync settings.
  3. Uncheck Export approved bills and recorded payments.
  4. Click Save sync settings.
  5. Check Export approved bills and recorded payments.
  6. Click Save sync settings again.
  7. Contact Clio's support team for additional steps.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (2050)

(2050)

This error code can be caused by any one of the following situations:

  • QuickBooks Online Error Code (2050) : Invalid ________. String length specified does not match the supported length. Min:0 Max: _____ supported. Supplied length: _____: Data included when creating the contact cannot be pulled over because there are too many characters. For example, a phone number on the contact card with over 21 characters can cause this error code.
  • QuickBooks Online Error Code (2050) : Invalid DocNumber. String length specified does not match the supported length: The bill invoice ID # is too long.
  • QuickBooks Online Error Code (2050): Invalid CustomerMemo. String length specified does not match the supported length: The CustomerMemo field refers to the total length of the matter numbers for each matter on a bill. If the total number of characters in the matter numbers on the bill exceed the 1,000 character limit, it can cause this error code. 

To resolve "QuickBooks Online Error Code (2050) : Invalid ________. String length specified does not match the supported length. Min:0 Max: _____ supported. Supplied length: _____," follow these steps:

  1. Adjust the number of characters in the specified field to be within the allowed amounts.

 

To resolve "QuickBooks Online Error Code (2050) : Invalid DocNumber. String length specified does not match the supported length," follow these steps:

  1. Edit the bill invoice ID # to shorten it.

 

To resolve QuickBooks Online Error Code (2050): Invalid CustomerMemo. String length specified does not match the supported length," follow these steps:

  1. Update your matter numbering scheme to ensure that the length of each matter number is short enough that the combined total equals less than 1,000 characters.

(2500)

This error code occurs when Clio attempts to sync to a QuickBooks Online record (e.g customer, class, journal entry) that has been deleted in QuickBooks Online. This error code can potentially be caused by any of the following situations:

  2. Click Retry on the QuickBooks Online error for the contact.
  3. In QuickBooks Online, merge the previously existing contact into the newly created contact.
    • You can merge contacts by editing the contact with the Clio ID in QuickBooks Online and copying the name in the Display name as field, and then pasting the copied name into the original contact's Display name as field. When you save the contact, you will be prompted to merge the contacts. Learn more here.

 

If you need to edit a contact in Clio and merge the contact in QuickBooks Online, follow these steps to resolve the error code:

  1. In Clio Manage, change the contact's name. This will create a new contact in QuickBooks Online.
  2. In QuickBooks Online, merge the old contact with the new contact.
    • You can merge contacts by editing the contact with the Clio ID in QuickBooks Online and copying the name in the Display name as field, and then pasting the copied name into the original contact's Display name as field. When you save the contact, you will be prompted to merge the contacts. Learn more here.

QuickBooks Online error code (6000)

(6000)

This error code will specify which information it is looking to adjust, such as payment, credit note, or tax, and it will not affect the sync. This error code can potentially be caused by any of the following situations:

  • A transaction was entered as $0.00 for a possible multi-matter bill where payment was entered for one matter but not others.

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  2. Activate the contact within QuickBooks Online.

  4. If you have a bill in Clio that uses a different currency, manually create bills that use alternate currencies in QuickBooks Online.
  5. Confirm that each line of taxation has a tax code. Global companies need a tax code at each line of taxation. Learn more here.
  6. If there is a bill with a negative balance that will not sync to QuickBooks online, change the bill to a positive balance. 
  7. If you have an invoice with multiple currencies, duplicate the contact in QuickBooks Online and assign a currency per contact.

QuickBooks Online error code (6140)

(6140)

This error code will occur when Clio attempts to sync an item (e.g. bill, payment, interest charge, credit note, journal entry, or something else) to QuickBooks Online but that number has already been used elsewhere in QuickBooks Online. It is possible that a duplicate number may not appear to exist in QuickBooks Online but the invoice number is still not accepted by QuickBooks Online.

Numbers in QuickBooks Online are required to be unique for the transaction type. For example, a bill in Clio cannot sync to QuickBooks Online if there is a credit memo in QuickBooks Online with the same number.

The error shown in Clio will give you clues toward what record in QuickBooks Online is conflicting with Clio. For example, here is a breakdown for "Code (6140): Duplicate Document Number Error : You must specify a different number. This number has already been used. DocNumber=1234 is assigned to TxnType=Credit Memo with TxnId=111":

  • DocNumber: This document number is used by Clio and already exists in QuickBooks Online. This number is causing the error.
  • TxnType: This is the type of record or transaction in QuickBooks Online that has the duplicate DocNumber Clio is trying to use.
  • TxnId: This is an ID number used by QuickBooks Online to identify the record. It can be found in the URL of the record in QuickBooks Online. For example, you can find a bill invoice with the TxnId as 123 at https://app.qbo.intuit.com/app/invoice?txnid=123 and a credit memo with the TxnId as 111 at https://app.qbo.intuit.com/app/creditmemo?txnid=111. To find other TxnId types, open the transaction of the same type in QuickBooks Online and change the txnId in the URL.

  

If bills in Clio are causing the error, try one of the following resolutions:

Option 1: Add a bill prefix in QuickBooks Online settings and then re-sync:

  1. In Clio Manage, go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  2. Click Configure Settings.
  3. Under Bill prefix, add a prefix.
  4. Click Save Sync Settings.
  5. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  6. Scroll down to find the error code and then click Retry.

Option 2: Edit the bill's number in Clio and then re-sync:

This option is not available if the error is caused by an interest charge in Clio. For interest charge error, follow options 1 or 3.

  1. Learn more here. 
  2. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  3. Scroll down to find the error code and then click Retry.

Option 3: Edit the bill invoice's number in QuickBooks Online and then re-sync:

  1. Learn more here. 
  2. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  3. Scroll down to find the error code and then click Retry.

 

If credit memos are causing the error, try the following resolution:

  1. Find the credit memo in QuickBooks Online and change the number in the Credit Memo no field.
  2. Go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  3. Scroll down to find the error code and then click Retry.

 

If trust transactions are causing the error, try the following resolution:

  1. In QuickBooks Online, do one of the following:
    • Select Settings > Advanced Settings. Disable Warn if duplicate journal number is used.
    • Manually add a new journal entry to your trust account and offsetting transaction to your Trust Liabilities account. Delete the journal entry that was added. 
  2. In Clio Manage, go to Settings > Bill Syncing.
  3. Scroll down to find the error code and then click Retry.
  4. Wait for the next sync cycle to re-sync.

  4. In QuickBooks Online, check that a new Class matching that name was created.
  5. Merge the old Class (the user with the unchanged name) with the newly created Class. Learn more here.
  6. In Clio, change the user's name back to the original name.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (6250)

(6250)

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • A contact in QuickBooks Online with an identical display name was archived. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Unarchive the customer in QuickBooks Online. Learn more here.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (6470)

(6470)

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • QuickBooks Online is attempting to calculate tax on Clio bills. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Remove an account-wide tax code from QuickBooks online to disable the Tax Centre from attempting to calculate tax on bills.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (6480)

(6480)

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • A firm disconnected a QuickBooks online account from Clio, connected a new account, and then attempted to edit a transaction. 

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Manually edit the QuickBooks Online transaction before reconciling to match any changes made in Clio.

 

QuickBooks Online error code (6540)

(6540)

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • QuickBooks online will not allow Clio to make changes to a synced payment that has already been deposited. A payment edited in Clio will be treated as being deleted and then reapplied with the edits when syncing to QuickBooks Online. Editing a payment that has been deposited will produce the same error. This can result in an additional payment being applied to the bill in QuickBooks Online.

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Go into QuickBooks Online and find the original linked payment/transaction that was deposited.
  2. Unlink the transaction/payment by changing or deleting it on QuickBooks Online from the bank account. 
    • The payment should return into the undeposited funds section in QuickBooks Online.
  3. Make necessary modifications in Clio if the payment needs to be reflected in QuickBooks Online.

 

QuickBooks Online error: At least 1 line item is required

At least 1 line item is required

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • All line items have been removed from the bill. QuickBooks Online requires bill to have at least one line item.

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Ignore the error. The bill will not sync to QuickBooks Online. OR
  2. Void the bill and generate a new bill with at least one line item.

 

QuickBooks Online error: Item-based line items

Item-based line items

This error code is caused by the following situation:

  • If a line item is in "Item Details" when the expense is imported to Clio, an error will appear in the Sync Failures table in Settings > Bill Syncing > QuickBooks Online Sync.

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. Remove the line item from the Item Details section in QuickBooks Online.
  2. Create a new expense and add the line item into the Category Details section to import the expense into Clio.
    • Do not move the same line item that previously existed in the Item Details section into the Category Details section. This will not fix the error.
  3. Wait for the expense to sync to Clio.

 

QuickBooks Online Sync Issue: Failed to import changes to Contact. Unable to update primary email address

Failed to import changes to Contact. Unable to update the primary email address

Other syncs will work as usual, but any change made to the specific contact in QuickBooks Online will not affect the Clio Manage contact until the sync failure is resolved. This error code is caused by any of the following situations:

  • Contacts in Clio Manage using Clio for Clients use their primary email address to log in. This means that two Clio Manage contacts using Clio for Clients cannot have the same primary email address.
  • When a change is made in QuickBooks Online to the contact's email address and these updates cannot be imported into Clio Manage, this sync failure will appear in the Sync Failures table.

To resolve this error code, follow these steps:

  1. In Clio Manage, change the contact's email address. OR
  2. In QuickBooks Online, change the contact's email address to a new email address.

results.name: Create Trust Requests
results.title: Create Trust Requests
results.body:
Trust requests let your firm collect an initial retainer or top up a matter when trust funds reach a minimum, so the funds are in place before you bill against them. Creating a trust request records the amount you are asking the client to deposit and where to store it, at the client or matter level.

Note: Create a trust account in Clio Manage before completing this procedure.

Understand trust requests and trust transactions

Trust requests and trust transactions are different tools. A request asks for funds and whereas the trust transaction can be recorded when the client pays.

Trust request

An ask for the client to deposit funds into your trust account, such as a retainer. Your firm will not receive payment until the client pays.

Trust transaction

A transaction recorded for accounting purposes showing funds were received and deposited in the trust account ledger, transferred into or our of a trust account, or that funds were disbursed.

 

Create a trust request

Trust requests aim to collect initial trust deposits or retainers or to request to the client that additional funds are added to a matter when the trust balance reaches a minimum. You can create a trust request from the contact or matter Dashboard, the main Billing tab, or the global Create new menu.

Note: You can store trust funds at the client or matter level and the trust request can reflect that. The trust request currency is determined by the billing preferences for the matter or the client.

  1. Go to a contact and click New trust request. Alternatively, click the global Create new + in the top right and select Trust request.
  2. Complete the trust request details.

  3. Optional: Select Skip the trust approval process if you want to be able to ready the trust request for sending without approval from another firm member.

    Important: Skipping the approval process locks the trust request from being edited after you generate it. To keep a request editable, leave the approval process in place.

  4. Click Save trust request.

 

Autofill trust request amounts

If you set up evergreen trust, autofill calculates the amount you need to request to reach the minimum trust balance required. Above the Amount field, select Autofill, then choose an option. You can override the amount before you send the request.

Note: Autofill options change only the request amount. A trust request shows a single total and does not itemize outstanding bills or work in progress. To explain the amount to your client, use Add a note.

Replenish to minimum

Tops up the trust balance to the matter threshold.

Replenish and outstanding balance

The matter threshold plus any unpaid bills.

Replenish, outstanding balance, and work in progress

The matter threshold plus unpaid bills plus unbilled work in progress.

  • Record Payments on Trust Requests: Record a payment on a trust request when your client pays.

results.name: Approve and Send Trust Requests
results.title: Approve and Send Trust Requests
results.body:
Approving and sending trust requests moves a request through your firm review process and delivers it to the client so they can deposit funds. Approval confirms the request internally, and sending issues it to the client by the method you choose. With a request approved and sent, the client can pay and you can record the deposit.

Approve a trust request

When a trust request is created without skipping the approval process, it appears in the Draft subtab in Billing. From there, you can submit the request for approval by another firm member or approve it directly.

Submit a trust request for approval

  1. Go to Billing, or the Bills tab in a contact or matter.
  2. Click the Draft subtab.
  3. Click the down arrow next to Edit and select Submit for approval.
  4. Select the firm members who need to approve the trust request.
  5. Under Notify via, select Email and/or Internal message to notify the firm members. 
  6. Optional: Click Add note to include a note with the approval request.
  7. Click Submit for approval.

 

Approve a trust request directly

  1. Go to Billing, or the Bills tab in a contact or matter.
  2. Click the Pending approval subtab.
  3. Click the down arrow next to Edit and select Approve trust request.

 

Send a trust request

After a trust request is approved, you can send it to the client. You can also send the request to other related contacts.

  1. Go to Billing, or the Bills tab in a contact or matter.
  2. Click the Unpaid subtab.
  3. Click Send.
  4. Select the trust bill template, make any changes, and select the send method.
  5. Click Send trust request.

Tip: If you are using Clio Payments, your client can pay the trust funds request amount directly from their billing email using a debit or credit card. Learn more about Clio Payments.

 

Up next

  • Manage Trust Requests: Find, edit, delete, or void an existing trust request.
